items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: It featured a tenor solo by Hershel Evans, a beautiful solo. And the tenor player learned this solo from listening to the record.

ctx.x: After that, one time I got the idea to write some whole notes behind... This record, "Muskrat Ramble"... I don't remember, it might have been Benny Goodman's group. It was a small group... No, Lionel Hampton. Lionel Hampton and I think Benny Goodman might have been on the record. But it featured a tenor solo by Hershel Evans, a beautiful solo. And the tenor player learned this solo from listening to the record. So what I did, I found out what the chords were, and I gave the band the chords to play behind him on…

So then I began to write out backgrounds for maybe the saxophones and have a trumpet player play a lead or something like that. It got so that where all the kids were starting their chords and everything, and we'd get... We had a system where in a chord, I would say somebody played a root, somebody else played a third and somebody else played a fifth, and I'd stand in front of the band and have somebody play the lead, and call the chords out to the brass section, and they'd take their respective notes and they'd…
